overview:
Casablanca is where most international flights land, and this private tour turns that arrival into the start of a complete journey across Morocco. In eight days you travel from the Atlantic to the Rif mountains, through the imperial city of Fes and the Roman ruins of Volubilis, over the Middle Atlas to a night in the Sahara, back west through the great gorges and the kasbah country, and over the High Atlas to Marrakech, where the tour ends in time for your flight home.

You begin with the Hassan II Mosque on the ocean and the royal capital, Rabat, then head north to Chefchaouen, the blue town of the Rif. On the way to Fes you walk among the mosaics of Volubilis, and in Fes a licensed guide spends a full day with you in the medina. From Fes you cross the cedar forests and high plateaus of the Middle Atlas to Merzouga, ride a camel into the Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset and sleep in a desert camp. The return west follows the Todra and Dades gorges and the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs to Ait Ben Haddou, then the Tizi n'Tichka pass to Marrakech, where a guided morning of palaces and souks closes the trip.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 8 days, 7 nights
• Start: Casablanca (Mohammed V airport, station or hotel) – Finish: Marrakech (hotel or Menara airport)
• Type: private tour with your own driver; licensed local guides in Fes and Marrakech, local guide at Volubilis
• Total distance: about 1,900 km; the long days are Fes–Merzouga (about 470 km) and Dades–Marrakech (about 340 km)
• Nights: Rabat, Chefchaouen, Fes (2), Erg Chebbi desert camp, Dades valley, Marrakech
• Meals: breakfast daily; dinner at the desert camp and in the Dades
• Activity level: easy to moderate

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Hassan II Mosque, one of the few in Morocco open to non-Muslims.
• Rabat's Kasbah of the Udayas, Hassan Tower and Mausoleum of Mohammed V.
• Chefchaouen's blue medina and the view from the Spanish Mosque.
• The Roman city of Volubilis, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
• Fes el-Bali: the Bou Inania and Attarine madrasas, the Qarawiyyin and the Chouara tannery.
• Ifrane, the cedar forest and its Barbary macaques, Midelt and the Ziz valley.
• The Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset and sunrise.
• The Todra and Dades gorges, the Valley of Roses and Ait Ben Haddou.
• Marrakech: the Koutoubia, the Bahia Palace, the souks and Jemaa el-Fna.

WHY THIS ITINERARY WORKS
Many desert tours start and end in Marrakech and skip the north. This one uses your Casablanca arrival to add Rabat, Chefchaouen, Volubilis and two nights in Fes, then finishes in Marrakech, where many flights home leave. The only backtracking is unavoidable – the desert is a long way from everything – and the long drives are broken by real stops.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
First-time visitors with about a week, couples, families with children over about eight, photographers and travellers flying into Casablanca and out of Marrakech.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
With a little more time, the [10-day grand tour from Casablanca](/en-US/morocco/casablanca/tours/10-day-grand-tour-of-morocco-from-casablanca-chefchaouen-fes-sahara-marrakech/bd1fc4fe0dad1d1f3c84b14e) adds a second desert night and a slower pace. For a shorter trip, see the [6-day desert express from Casablanca](/en-US/morocco/casablanca/tours/6-day-desert-express-from-casablanca-marrakech-sahara-camp-fes/2ab41e5f1e7059708feeb5c3).

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Bring layers for the mountains and cold desert nights (close to freezing from December to February), sun protection, a small bag for the camp night and modest clothing for the Hassan II Mosque. Entrance fees, lunches and the dinners not listed are not included; most sites cost 30 to 120 dirhams. Tell us your flight times so the first and last days fit them.
descriptions:
What to expect: arrival in Casablanca, the Hassan II Mosque on the ocean, and an afternoon in Rabat, the royal capital.

Your driver meets you at Mohammed V airport or your hotel. The first visit is the Hassan II Mosque, completed in 1993 on a platform over the Atlantic, with a minaret of about 210 m and a prayer hall for 25,000 worshippers under a partly retractable cedar roof; guided tours show the hall, the marble ablution rooms and the hammam below. After lunch you drive an hour north to Rabat. Walk up through the blue-and-white lanes of the Kasbah of the Udayas to its terrace over the mouth of the Bou Regreg and the Andalusian garden, then visit the Hassan Tower, the unfinished minaret of a 12th-century mosque standing among the stumps of its columns, and the white Mausoleum of Mohammed V opposite, with its royal guards. Evening free in Rabat.

SCHEDULE (times depend on your arrival)
Arrival – Pick-up at the airport or your hotel.
11:00 – Hassan II Mosque guided visit (about 1 hour).
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
14:30 – Drive to Rabat (about 1 hour).
15:30 – Kasbah of the Udayas, Hassan Tower and Mausoleum.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Mosque visits need covered shoulders and knees; there are none on Friday mornings. If you land late, we visit the mosque on the way out of Casablanca or skip it.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, airport pick-up, hotel with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: mosque ticket, meals, tips.

Overnight: hotel in Rabat.
Meals: none (breakfast the next morning).

What to expect: north through farmland and the Rif foothills to Chefchaouen, the blue town, with sunset from the Spanish Mosque.

The drive north takes about four hours through the rich plains of the Gharb, with sugar cane, citrus orchards and the market town of Ouezzane, before climbing into the Rif. Chefchaouen was founded in 1471 on the slopes of the Jebel Kelaa and became a refuge for Muslims and Jews from Andalusia; its lanes, washed in every shade of blue, are among the most photographed in Morocco. After lunch on the Outa el-Hammam square, explore the kasbah and its garden, the stepped alleys of the Souika quarter and the Ras el-Maa spring, where women still wash wool. In the late afternoon walk up the path to the Spanish Mosque, about 30 minutes, for the sunset over the town and the mountains.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Depart Rabat.
13:00 – Arrival in Chefchaouen; lunch (not included).
15:00 – Walk in the blue medina and the kasbah.
17:30 – Spanish Mosque for sunset.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Riads are inside the medina; your driver parks at the gate and porters carry your luggage.
• Ask before photographing people; many residents prefer not to be photographed.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: meals, tips.

Overnight: riad in Chefchaouen.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: an early walk in the empty blue lanes, then south to the Roman city of Volubilis and on to Fes.

Take an early stroll in Chefchaouen while the light is soft and the lanes are quiet, then drive south through olive groves and rolling hills. Volubilis, about three hours away, is the best-preserved Roman site in Morocco and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. With a local guide you walk the main street, the Decumanus Maximus, under the triumphal arch built for Emperor Caracalla, past the basilica and the capitol, and into the houses where floor mosaics still lie in place: Orpheus charming the animals, Bacchus, the Labours of Hercules. Across the valley rises Moulay Idriss, the holy town where the founder of Morocco's first Islamic dynasty is buried. You reach Fes in the late afternoon and settle into your riad.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:00 – Early walk in Chefchaouen (optional).
09:00 – Depart.
12:00 – Volubilis with a local guide (about 1.5 hours).
13:30 – Lunch (not included).
14:45 – Moulay Idriss viewpoint.
16:00 – Arrival in Fes.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Volubilis has almost no shade: bring a hat and water.
• If you prefer, we can add a short stop at Meknes to see the Bab Mansour gate.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, local guide at Volubilis, riad or hotel with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fee, lunch, tips.

Overnight: riad or hotel in Fes.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a full day in the largest car-free medina in the world, with a licensed guide who knows its lanes.

Fes el-Bali was founded in the 9th century and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Your guide starts outside the walls at the golden doors of the Royal Palace and in the Mellah, the old Jewish quarter, then enters the medina through Bab Boujloud, the blue gate. You visit the Bou Inania madrasa, with its carved cedar, stucco and zellige, walk down the Talaa Kebira through the souks of spices, leather and brass, and see the courtyard of the Qarawiyyin from its doors – founded in 859 by Fatima al-Fihri, it is often called the oldest existing university in the world – before visiting the smaller Attarine madrasa next to it. You pass the Nejjarine fountain, the coppersmiths of the Seffarine square and the weavers, and end on a terrace above the Chouara tannery, where hides are still dyed in stone vats. At the end of the day your driver can take you to the Merinid tombs for the view over the whole city.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Royal Palace gates and the Mellah.
10:00 – Bab Boujloud and the Bou Inania madrasa.
11:30 – The souks.
13:00 – Lunch in the medina (not included).
14:30 – Qarawiyyin, Attarine madrasa and the Seffarine square.
15:30 – Chouara tannery terraces.
17:00 – Merinid tombs viewpoint (optional).

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Qarawiyyin mosque is closed to non-Muslims.
• Guides take you into workshops; there is never an obligation to buy.

INCLUDED: licensed local guide, riad or hotel with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

Overnight: riad or hotel in Fes.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: the long, beautiful drive over the Middle Atlas to the edge of the Sahara, and a camel ride into the Erg Chebbi for a night in a desert camp.

You leave Fes early and climb to Ifrane, a town of sloping roofs built in an alpine style at 1,650 m, then into the cedar forest near Azrou, where Barbary macaques live wild among the trees. The road crosses high plateaus to Midelt, the apple town under the Jebel Ayachi, and over the Tizi n'Talghemt pass, then drops into the Ziz gorges and follows a long ribbon of palm groves past Errachidia and Erfoud. In the late afternoon you reach the dunes near Merzouga. Leave your main luggage in the vehicle and ride a camel for about an hour and a half into the Erg Chebbi as the sand turns orange, climb a dune for the sunset and arrive at your camp for dinner, drums by the fire and a sky full of stars.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:00 – Depart Fes.
09:00 – Ifrane and the cedar forest with the macaques.
13:00 – Lunch in Midelt (not included).
15:00 – Ziz valley viewpoint.
17:00 – Camel ride into the Erg Chebbi (about 1.5 hours).
19:00 – Desert camp; dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 470 km; your driver stops whenever you like.
• Pack a small bag for the camp: warm layer, torch, toothbrush.
• Camps with private bathrooms in each tent are available on request.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, camel ride, desert camp with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: desert camp in the Erg Chebbi.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: sunrise over the dunes, then west along the edge of the desert to the Todra gorge and up the Dades valley.

Wake before dawn to climb a dune and watch the sun rise over the Sahara, then ride back to Merzouga for a shower and breakfast. The road west passes the ksour of Rissani and the oasis of Tinejdad with its khettaras, lines of wells marking ancient underground water channels. At Tinghir you look over one of the longest palm groves of the south before driving into the Todra gorge, where the limestone walls rise about 300 m and close to around ten metres apart; walk along the stream through the narrows. In the afternoon continue to Boumalne and up the Dades valley, past the rounded red rocks called the 'monkey fingers' and the hairpin road of Tisdrine, to your hotel above the river.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00 – Sunrise from the dunes; camel ride back.
08:30 – Shower, breakfast and departure.
11:30 – Todra gorge walk (about 1 hour).
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
16:00 – Dades valley and the Tisdrine viewpoint.
17:30 – Hotel in the Dades; dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The gorge floor is flat; wear shoes you can get wet if you want to paddle.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel in the Dades valley.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs, the fortified village of Ait Ben Haddou and the crossing of the High Atlas to Marrakech.

The road west passes Kelaat M'Gouna in the Valley of Roses, where small Damask roses are picked in spring and distilled into rose water, the palm grove of Skoura and the town of Ouarzazate. Around midday you reach Ait Ben Haddou, a ksar of earthen houses and towers climbing a hill above the Ounila river, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987 and a setting for many films; walk across the river and up through its lanes to the granary at the top. In the afternoon the road climbs to the Tizi n'Tichka, at about 2,260 m the highest main road pass in Morocco, with views over terraced Berber villages, before descending through the foothills to Marrakech in the early evening.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:00 – Depart the Dades; Valley of Roses and Skoura.
11:30 – Ait Ben Haddou (about 1 hour).
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
14:30 – Tizi n'Tichka pass with viewpoints.
18:00 – Arrival in Marrakech.

GOOD TO KNOW
• This is a long day of about 340 km; the Tichka road has many bends.
• A local guide at Ait Ben Haddou can be added on request.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, riad or hotel with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, entrance fees, tips.

Overnight: riad or hotel in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a guided morning in Marrakech – the Koutoubia, the Bahia Palace, the souks and Jemaa el-Fna – and the end of the tour at your hotel or the airport.

Your guide meets you after breakfast. Start at the Koutoubia, whose 12th-century minaret is the landmark of the city, then visit the Bahia Palace, built in the late 19th century for a grand vizier, with its courtyards, gardens and painted cedar ceilings. If time allows, see the Saadian Tombs, sealed for centuries and rediscovered in 1917. Then cross the souks – spices, leather, lanterns, carpets – to Jemaa el-Fna, the great square at the heart of the medina. The guided tour ends around midday. Your driver then takes you to Marrakech Menara airport or your hotel if you are staying longer.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Koutoubia and Bahia Palace.
10:30 – Saadian Tombs (if time allows).
11:00 – The souks and Jemaa el-Fna.
12:30 – End of the guided tour; transfer to the airport or your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• For an afternoon flight, allow at least two hours at the airport.
• If you stay longer, we can book the Majorelle Garden for the afternoon.

INCLUDED: licensed local guide, final transfer.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

Overnight: none (end of the tour).
Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: Can you pick us up at Casablanca airport?
faq.answer: Yes. Your driver meets you at Mohammed V airport, the train station or your hotel, whatever time your flight lands.

faq.question: Where does the tour end?
faq.answer: In Marrakech, around midday on Day 8 after the guided morning, at your hotel or Marrakech Menara airport.

faq.question: Is the tour private?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle, driver and guides are only for you and your group, and you can change stops and timings each day.

faq.question: How many nights in the desert?
faq.answer: One night in a desert camp in the Erg Chebbi dunes. If you would like a second night or a full day in the Sahara, the 10-day tour from Casablanca includes it, or we can add a day.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Breakfast every day, plus dinner at the desert camp and in the Dades valley. Other meals are not included so you can choose where to eat.

faq.question: Are guides included?
faq.answer: Yes: a licensed guide for a full day in Fes and a morning in Marrakech, and a local guide at Volubilis. Your driver explains the sights along the way.

faq.question: Which are the long driving days?
faq.answer: Fes to Merzouga (about 470 km) and the Dades to Marrakech (about 340 km). Both have regular stops at viewpoints and towns, and the vehicle is air-conditioned.

faq.question: What is the desert camp like?
faq.answer: Berber-style tents in the Erg Chebbi with real beds, blankets, dinner and breakfast. Camps with private bathrooms in each tent are available on request.

faq.question: What kind of accommodation is used?
faq.answer: Hotels in Rabat and the Dades, riads in Chefchaouen, Fes and Marrakech, and one night in a desert camp. You can choose standard, superior or luxury when you book.

faq.question: Are entrance fees included?
faq.answer: No. They are paid on the day and are modest: most sites cost 30 to 120 dirhams, the Hassan II Mosque a little more.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children comfortable with a few long drives, usually from about eight. Child seats are available on request.

faq.question: When is the best time for this tour?
faq.answer: Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November). Winter is fine with warm clothes for the desert night; July and August are very hot in the south.

faq.question: Can the tour start in Marrakech instead?
faq.answer: Yes. We can run the same route in reverse, from Marrakech to Casablanca, or adapt it to your flights. Tell us when you book.
